citations.reference: Taher AT, Weatherall DJ, Cappellini MD. Thalassaemia. Lancet. 2018;391(10116):155-167.
citations.key_findings: Beta-thalassemia trait presents with microcytosis and mild or no anemia. MCV is typically between 60-70 fL.

citations.reference: Cao A, Galanello R. Beta-thalassemia. Genetics in Medicine. 2010;12(2):61-76.
citations.key_findings: Mentzer index (MCV/RBC) less than 13 suggests beta-thalassemia trait rather than iron deficiency.

citations.reference: Camaschella C. Iron-deficiency anemia. New England Journal of Medicine. 2015;372(19):1832-1843.
citations.key_findings: Iron deficiency anemia typically presents with low MCV, low MCH, elevated RDW, and low ferritin.

citations.reference: Naik RP, Haywood C. Sickle cell trait diagnosis: clinical and social implications. Hematology. 2015;2015(1):160-167.
citations.key_findings: Sickle cell trait is generally asymptomatic but can be identified by hemoglobin electrophoresis showing HbS less than 50%.

citations.reference: Vichinsky E. Hemoglobin E syndromes. Hematology. 2007;2007(1):79-83.
citations.key_findings: HbE trait presents with microcytosis out of proportion to anemia, similar to beta-thalassemia trait.

citations.reference: World Health Organization. Laboratory reference ranges. WHO Guidelines. 2021.
citations.key_findings: Laboratory values within normal reference ranges suggest absence of disease.

citations.reference: Hickner J, et al. Testing for uncommon conditions. American Family Physician. 2019;99(8):490-496.
citations.key_findings: When lab patterns do not match common conditions, further diagnostic testing is indicated.
